conj:casimir-first-q-correction:
Conjecture First aether correction to the Casimir force is carried by the figure-eight knot 4_1. Assume the plate-constrained mode-count of Casimir force. Its leading 1/d^{4} term is built from disjoint free-photon modes and is independent of aether deformation. The first contribution carrying aether-q dependence arises from the interacting sector.   J_{4_1}(q) = q^{-2} - q^{-1} + 1 - q + q^{2} = 1 + \tfrac{3}{4}h^{2} + O(h^{4}), \qquad h = q - q^{-1}.

The leading parallel-plate term is assembled from free photon modes (identity braids). Degree-\leq 1 closures are non-hyperbolic with vanishing volume. Modes that do not braid transmit no aether deformation. Aether corrections enter only where modes braid.

Degree \geq 2 is necessary for hyperbolicity. Minimal degree-\geq 2 closures (Hopf link, trefoil, (2,5)-torus knot) have \mathrm{Vol} = 0. The first hyperbolic closure is the figure-eight knot 4_1, with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299.

The figure-eight weight satisfies the exact field identity

  J_{4_1}(q) = 1 + \tfrac{3}{4}h^{2} + \frac{h^{4}}{4(h^{2} + 8 + 4(q + q^{-1}))}.

The coefficient 3/4 is forced by the identity.

The aether parameter q_0 is fixed through \mathrm{Vol}(4_1). The knot defining the one calibrated deformation parameter also carries the vacuum's first aether correction.

The conjecture requires the interacting-mode mode-sum. The 1/d^6 power is an expectation, not a derivation. The absolute magnitude is suppressed by \sim \alpha \lambda_C/d, below current precision. Falsification requires showing the first non-vanishing aether correction is not weighted by J_{4_1}.

conj:local-infinitesimal-field:
Conjecture Aether parameter as a local infinitesimal field \varepsilon(x). The appendix so far treats the aether parameter q = 1 + \varepsilon as a single global element of the valuation ring \mathcal{O} \subset \mathbf{No}. This conjecture proposes a richer structure: \varepsilon is a sheaf of infinitesimals across a scheme X, with q(x) = 1 + \varepsilon(x) varying locally from patch to patch.

Setup

Let X be the scheme of quantum observable universes (underlying the categorical aether of this paper). Following the points-and-topology framework already in the paper, treat X as a functor \mathrm{CRing} \to \mathrm{Set}.

Evaluate X at the valuation ring (valuation ring of finite surreals):

  X(\mathcal{O})
   := \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(\mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}).

An element of X(\mathcal{O}) is a "surreal-valued point" — an assignment of a finite surreal to each coordinate of X. The standard-part map \mathrm{st} : \mathcal{O} \to \mathbb{R} induces

  X(\mathrm{st}) \;:\; X(\mathcal{O}) \twoheadrightarrow X(\mathbb{R}),

sending each surreal-valued point to its classical real shadow by stripping infinitesimal fluctuations.

Conjecture

The aether parameter is not a global constant q \in \mathbb{R} but a section of the structure sheaf valued in \mathcal{O}:

  \varepsilon \;\in\; \Gamma(X, \mathfrak{m}_X),

where \mathfrak{m}_X \subset \mathcal{O}_X is the sheaf of infinitesimals on X(\mathcal{O}). Writing \varepsilon(x) for the stalk at a point x \in X:

  1. Local variation: \varepsilon(x) may differ from \varepsilon(y) for distinct x, y \in X — the aether parameter fluctuates across the scheme.

  2. Standard-part global constant: \mathrm{st}(\varepsilon(x)) = 0 for all x, so the classical aether is q_{\mathrm{classical}} = 1 everywhere — matching the archimedean limit to a trivial constant.

  3. Birthday-uniform at archimedean scale: the leading surreal coefficient of \varepsilon(x) (i.e., the coefficient of \omega^{-1} in the Conway normal form) is globally constant, and equals the paper's archimedean aether deviation q_0 - 1 \approx 0.11.

Equivalently, q(x) = 1 + (q_0 - 1) + \delta(x) where \delta(x) is a strictly-infinitesimal local fluctuation with zero mean and birthday-ordered magnitude distribution.

Significance

  1. Halo structure: every classical real point of X is surrounded by a halo (monad) of infinitesimally-fluctuated surreal points. Under the functor X(\mathrm{st}) all halo points collapse to the classical point — but within the halo, distinct surreal fluctuations are resolved.

  2. Non-global symmetries: a symmetry of this paper's QOU that is global in the archimedean sense may be broken at the infinitesimal scale locally (at specific points x), without affecting the classical image. This is analogous to approximate isospin / chiral symmetries in particle physics.

  3. Singularity detection: a "singularity" of this paper's QOU is a point x_0 where some quantity diverges. In the surreal lift, the divergence has a specific normal-form order \ordw(\cdot) — which, by locality, can vary in a neighbourhood of x_0.

Relation to existing conjectures

This conjecture refines Hahn-series aether: instead of q being a single Hahn series, it is a sheaf of Hahn series. The base \mathbb{R}- shadow agrees with the paper in both cases.

It also specialises archimedean-stpart to the sheaf-theoretic setting: the archimedean QOU is the standard-part sheaf-morphism of the surreal QOU, not a single-point morphism.

Proof strategy

Mathematical layer (existence of local sheaf structure):

  1. Show that \mathcal{O} is a valid coefficient ring for the scheme X: it is a local ring, hence satisfies all standard sheaf-construction axioms (easy).

  2. Define \mathfrak{m}_X as the kernel sheaf of the structure- sheaf morphism \mathcal{O}_X \to (\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{m})_X = \mathbb{R}_X. This is the standard construction of an ideal sheaf.

  3. Verify that global sections of \mathfrak{m}_X exist (non-vacuously): the constant section \varepsilon \mapsto \varepsilon witnesses this.

  4. Characterise which global sections give consistent QOU structure — i.e., which \varepsilon-valued q deformations preserve the rigid monoidal axioms.

Physical layer (uniqueness of the fluctuation distribution):

  1. Assume the fluctuation distribution \delta(x) has some explicit form (e.g., zero-mean Gaussian on the classical spectrum of X).

  2. Show that the classical observables (particle masses, \mathcal{Q}-values, spectral gaps) are unchanged under standard-part — equivalent to the sheaf being \mathrm{st}- compatible.

  3. Show that there are no non-trivial fluctuation distributions at leading order beyond the global one — equivalent to rigidity of this paper QOU.

Falsification path: produce two distinct sheaf sections \varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2 on X both producing the same archimedean QOU under X(\mathrm{st}) but differing in some surreal observable (e.g., the second-order coefficient of a particle mass). Such non-uniqueness would show that the surreal lift is strictly richer than the archimedean, and the extra information is physical.

Provability assessment: mathematical layer provable once the finite-surreal valuation-ring foundations are developed. Physical layer speculative — depends on interpretation.
conj:spectral-normal-form:
Conjecture Spectral gap closure and singularity formation as q \to 1 read from normal-form exponents. Under the surreal lift q = 1 + \varepsilon (Hahn aether), every spectral operator O_q of this paper (Hecke generators, transfer matrices, q- Hamiltonians, Feynman integrals, vortex operators) has eigenvalues \lambda_i(q) that are rational in \varepsilon, hence elements of the valuation ring \mathcal{O}.

This conjecture asserts that spectral gaps and singularities as q \to 1 are read directly off the leading exponent \ordw(\cdot) of the eigenvalues, without analytic limits.

Conjecture

Let O_q : V \to V be a linear operator on a finite-dimensional \mathbf{No}-vector space, whose matrix entries are rational functions of q. At q = 1 + \varepsilon, let

  \lambda_1(\varepsilon) \leq \lambda_2(\varepsilon) \leq \cdots
   \leq \lambda_N(\varepsilon)

be the eigenvalues ordered by \mathbf{No}-magnitude. Define the spectral gap \Delta := \lambda_2(\varepsilon) - \lambda_1(\varepsilon).

  1. Algebraic closure at q = 1: the gap \Delta closes in the classical limit iff \ordw(\Delta) < 0 (i.e., \Delta is infinitesimal).

  2. Closure rate from leading exponent: the rate of closure is \ordw(\Delta) \in \mathbf{No}. Specifically:

    • \ordw(\Delta) = 0: gap stays open in the classical limit (no closure).
    • \ordw(\Delta) = -1: gap closes linearly, \Delta \sim c\,\varepsilon — generic first-order closure.
    • \ordw(\Delta) = -n for n \in \mathbb{N}: gap closes polynomially of order n.
    • \ordw(\Delta) \in (-\omega\cdot 2,\, -\omega): gap closes faster than any polynomial but slower than any exponential — signals transcendental quantum-dilogarithm behaviour.

  3. Singularity formation: a divergence (eigenvalue blowing up) has \ordw(\lambda_i) > 0 in the surreal lift. The exponent \ordw(\lambda_i) classifies the divergence type:

    • \ordw(\lambda_i) = 1: simple pole, \lambda_i \sim C/\varepsilon = C\omega.
    • \ordw(\lambda_i) = n: n-th order pole, \lambda_i \sim C\omega^n.
    • \ordw(\lambda_i) \in (1, 2): fractional-order divergence, signalling root-of-unity or Weierstrass behaviour.

  4. Algebraic vs transcendental singularities: if \ordw(\lambda_i) is a rational surreal (in the Hahn-series rationals \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbf{No}), the singularity is algebraic. If \ordw(\lambda_i) is transfinite (involves \omega or logarithms), the singularity is transcendental.

Application to QOU

Specialise to two main-paper operators:

Categorical transfer matrix T(c, d) (braiding eigenvalues):

  • Eigenvalues are q and -q^{-1} at every Hecke-level step.
  • At q = 1 + \varepsilon: leading terms 1 + \varepsilon and -(1 - \varepsilon + \varepsilon^2 - \cdots) = -1 + \varepsilon - \varepsilon^2 + \cdots.
  • Gap \Delta = q - (-q^{-1}) = q + q^{-1}, which equals 2 + O(\varepsilon^2) at q = 1 + \varepsilon. \ordw(\Delta - 2) = -2, so no closure; the classical limit preserves the binary splitting.

q-Hamiltonian \hat{H}_q (from this paper):

  • At q = 1 + \varepsilon, each eigenvalue is rational in \varepsilon.
  • Classical-limit q \to 1 eigenvalues are the standard-parts.
  • Quantum corrections are the subleading coefficients — accessible by inverting the \ordw filtration.

Möbius energy E_q:

  • E_q = \frac{1}{4} E_{\mathrm{classical}} + \mathrm{const} at q \to 1.
  • Surreal-lifted: \ordw(E_q - \frac{1}{4}E_{\mathrm{classical}}) \geq 0, with the leading surreal constant fixed.

Contrast with classical spectral theory

Classical spectral analysis of q-deformed operators requires:

  • \varepsilon--\delta bounds on eigenvalues as q \to 1;
  • careful treatment of multiplicity crossings;
  • perturbation theory with analytic convergence radii.

Under the surreal lift, all of this is replaced by:

  • algebraic evaluation of eigenvalues at q = 1 + \varepsilon (a rational arithmetic in \varepsilon);
  • ordinal-valued leading exponents of spectral differences classifying gap closure;
  • no convergence requirement — everything is formal power series with infinite-birthday exponents.

This is a substantive conceptual simplification; whether it corresponds to a practical proof technique (replacing current spectral-gap proofs in the paper with surreal evaluations) depends on computability of the normal forms.

Proof strategy

Algebraic case (provable now, modulo conjecture Hahn-aether):

  1. Assume O_q has matrix entries in \mathbb{Q}(q) or, more generally, in the Hahn-series aether.

  2. Eigenvalues are rational functions of q by standard linear algebra; hence rational in \varepsilon at q = 1 + \varepsilon.

  3. Compute \ordw(\Delta) directly from the rational-function expression.

  4. Verify against this paper's spectral-gap statements (e.g., for the Hecke generators where the gap is known classically).

Transcendental case (speculative):

  1. For operators whose entries involve the quantum dilogarithm or other transcendentals, appeal to Berarducci–Mantova exponential/log on \mathbf{No} [berarducci-mantova2018].

  2. Compute the normal-form expansion of each eigenvalue, reading off the leading transfinite exponent.

  3. Match against known asymptotic-volume formulas (Kashaev, etc.).

Required infrastructure:

  • Rational-function arithmetic at q = 1 + \varepsilon (partial; via specialising polynomials over R_q at surreal values).
  • Hahn-series aether (pending).
  • Normal-form computation for eigenvalues (pending).

Falsification path: find an operator O_q with classically well-defined spectral gap closure not matching the leading exponent \ordw(\Delta). Such a mismatch would refute the surreal-normal-form interpretation, likely indicating a subtle multi-scale behaviour that the surreal lift does not capture.

Provability assessment: algebraic case mostly tractable with current surreal infrastructure. Transcendental case requires Berarducci–Mantova. The overall conjecture is a dictionary, more testable than deep-research-open.

Open problem

The conjecture is open. Its importance depends on whether the QOU paper's spectral-gap and singularity-formation claims can be rewritten as leading-exponent computations. If so, the classical-limit discussions simplify substantially; if not, the surreal lift is a curiosity.
conj:kashaev-surreal:
Conjecture Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture as a surreal standard-part identity. The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture [kashaev1997] (open in full generality; provenance is recorded in that block) states:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
   \;=\; 2 \pi \cdot \lim_{n \to \infty}
    \frac{\log |J_K(\zeta_n, n)|}{n},

where J_K(q, n) is the n-th coloured Jones polynomial, \zeta_n = e^{2 \pi i / n}, and \mathrm{Vol} is the hyperbolic volume.

The conjecture has two awkward features when viewed through QOU:

  1. The left-hand side is hyperbolic volume — pure analytic geometry, broken under surreal replacement.
  2. The right-hand side uses an asymptotic-n limit at a root of unity — a singular limit in \mathbb{C}.

Under the surreal lift, both sides admit cleaner reformulations, and the gap between them sharpens.

Reformulation

Set n = \omega \in \mathbf{No} (the first infinite ordinal as a surreal). Then \zeta_\omega = e^{2 \pi i / \omega} is a specific element of \mathbf{No}[i] (interpreting the exponential via Berarducci--Mantova's transseries [berarducci-mantova2018]). The coloured Jones polynomial J_K(q, n) is rational in q and polynomial in n for fixed K, so J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega) is well-defined as an element of \mathbf{No}[i].

The surreal Kashaev statement is:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
   \;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
   \mathrm{st}\!\left(
     2 \pi \cdot \frac{\log |J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega)|}{\omega}
   \right),

where \mathrm{st} is the standard-part map applied to a finite surreal.

The trade-off

The reformulation does not solve the volume conjecture. It trades:

  • (classical) an analytic limit \lim_{n \to \infty} of complex numbers, plus a hyperbolic-volume identity in \mathbb{R};

for:

  • (surreal) an evaluation of a polynomial-in-n at n = \omega, plus the standard-part identity that the result agrees with hyperbolic volume.

The right-hand side of the surreal version is manifestly well-defined (rational arithmetic in \mathbf{No}), so the question reduces to whether the standard-part matches. The asymptotic-limit content of Kashaev becomes the standard-part content of the surreal version.

Location of the algebra-vs-analysis split

The reformulation makes the algebraic and analytic content of Kashaev separable:

Side Algebra-vs-analysis content
RHS, before \mathrm{st} Pure algebra: rational in \omega at root of unity
\mathrm{st} application Asymptotic transseries reduction
Identification with \mathrm{Vol} Genuine hyperbolic geometry

The first row uses no analysis. The second row uses a single transseries reduction (Berarducci--Mantova) — an instance of the \mathrm{st}/\mathrm{ord}_\omega reduction of the surreal blow-up calculus. The third row is where hyperbolic geometry enters — and it enters only on the LHS.

The second row admits a precise name from resurgence theory [ecalle1981]. The Berarducci--Mantova transseries invoked there are transseries in Écalle's sense, and the evaluation sits on a Stokes ray of the Kashaev asymptotic series, where the two lateral Borel sums of a divergent transseries disagree. The standard-part map applied to the finite surreal selects the unique real-single-valued value — which is the median resummation of Écalle's alien calculus. The unspecified "asymptotic transseries reduction" is therefore a named operation: \mathrm{st} acts as median resummation of the Kashaev transseries at the root of unity. This identifies the second row's content with a standard resurgence construction; it does not touch the third row, which remains the genuine geometric input.

The resummation step of the second row is proved for two families. For a Habiro element \Phi_K with formal series F_K(x) = \Phi_K(e^{-1/x}), the Costin--Garoufalidis conjecture asks that the Borel transform be resurgent and that the median resummation S^{\mathrm{med}}_K have radial limits recovering \Phi_K at roots of unity [crew2023, §1, Conj. 1.1]; it is proved for the torus knots T(2,2u+1) and T(3,2^k), which include the trefoil [crew2023, Cor. 1.5, via Thm. 1.4 and eq. (1.22)]. Torus knots have zero hyperbolic volume, so these cases bear on the second row only and say nothing about the \mathrm{Vol}-identity of the third row; 4_1 is outside the proved class.

Kashaev thus becomes one transseries reduction plus one \mathrm{Vol}-identity, instead of an analytic limit plus a \mathrm{Vol}-identity.

Potential utility and its limits

Might help: the algebraic side J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega) is exactly computable for any specific knot (it is a rational function evaluated at named surreals). If a general formula exists for \mathrm{st}(\log |J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega)|/\omega) in terms of knot data, there is a path to a proof of Kashaev.

Might not help: the standard-part identity is itself an analytic statement (it asserts an asymptotic relationship between the algebraic and the geometric). The surreal lift may just relocate the difficulty rather than dissolve it.

Discussion

Open in general; a theorem for the figure-eight knot — the conjecture is a reformulation, not a proof. Its value is in separating the algebraic content (which is computable) from the geometric content (which is the actual Kashaev). For K = 4_1 the classical limit statement is a theorem [murakami-murakami2001], so the surreal form holds with = in place of \stackrel{?}{=} for 4_1 — see the next section.

Figure-eight discharge and quantum-modularity refinement

For the figure-eight knot the two question marks collapse:

  1. Leading order (=, not \stackrel{?}{=}). The classical Kashaev limit for 4_1 is proved [murakami-murakami2001]. Combined with the formulation equivalence (proof-strategy items 1--3 below, provable by transfer), the surreal statement is a theorem for 4_1:

      \mathrm{st}\!\left(
    2 \pi \cdot \frac{\log |J_{4_1}(\zeta_\omega, \omega)|}{\omega}
  \right)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus 4_1)
  \;=\; 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3),

    conditional only on the transfer equivalence, not on any open conjecture.

  2. All orders (quantum modularity). Garoufalidis--Zagier [garoufalidis-zagier-2024] refine the leading asymptotic to a matrix-valued \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})-cocycle W_\gamma, holomorphic on cut planes, whose functional equation holds exactly — the factorially divergent perturbative series \Phi(\hbar) is the asymptotic expansion of an actual analytic object satisfying an equality, not merely an estimate.

  3. Stokes data as integer counts. The resurgent structure of the 4_1 Kashaev series is completely described in [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]: Borel singularities sit on the complex-volume lattice and the Stokes constants are organised as integer q-series identified with 3d-index data. Under the modular-resurgence template [fantini-rella2024] these Stokes constants are coefficients of an L-function, tying the alien calculus of the series to a quantum modular form.

The upgrade is deliberately scoped: it discharges the 4_1 instance of the surreal Kashaev statement and equips it with an exact (rather than asymptotic) analytic backbone. The general-knot statement remains open, exactly as for the classical volume conjecture. The QOU relevance is concentrated at 4_1 because the muon anchor is \mathfrak{m}_\mu = \mathfrak{m}_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2: the volume entering the mass formula is backed, at 4_1, by a proved equality rather than a conjectural limit.

What \mathrm{st} discards: the \omega-grade of the remainder

The sections above are thorough about what \mathrm{st} is and say nothing about what it throws away. For 4_1 the discarded quantity can be named exactly, and it is not a benign tail.

Following the surreal-equality bookkeeping of the blow-up calculus, write the pre-standard-part argument as \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) + \delta, i.e.

  \delta_N \;:=\;
   \frac{2\pi}{N}\,\log \langle 4_1 \rangle_N \;-\; \mathrm{Vol}(4_1),

with \langle 4_1 \rangle_N the Kashaev invariant, so that the discharge of the previous section is the statement \mathrm{st}(\delta) = 0 at N = \omega. Here \delta is the blow-up calculus's remainder symbol.

The grade, derived

The corpus derives the sub-leading shape of the Kashaev invariant at 4_1 from the saddle point, rather than importing it: at the one-variable saddle \theta^\ast = 5\pi/6 the Stirling factor is 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1 and the Hessian is |\cot\theta^\ast| = \sqrt{3}, giving

  \langle 4_1 \rangle_N \;\sim\; 3^{-1/4}\,N^{3/2}\,
   e^{\,N\,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/2\pi}

with both 3^{-1/4} and the power 3/2 derived (1-loop prefactor provenance). Taking logarithms term by term gives the two leading terms of the remainder:

  \delta_N \;=\; \frac{3\pi \log N}{N}
   \;-\; \frac{\pi \log 3}{2N} \;+\; r_N ,

since (2\pi/N)\cdot\tfrac{3}{2}\log N = 3\pi \log N / N and (2\pi/N)\cdot(-\tfrac{1}{4}\log 3) = -\pi \log 3 / (2N). The two named terms are derived; the order of r_N is not. A relative correction 1 + O(1/N) in the asymptotic above would give r_N = O(1/N^2), and check 1 of the probe below measures exactly that — the residual after subtracting the two terms falls by a factor 0.4928, 0.4966, 0.4983, 0.4992, 0.4996 on successive doublings, against 1/2 for a clean 1/N relative tail. That rate is measured here, not derived; the proposition cited above states the leading asymptotic and records the step from its two proved analytic inputs to the saddle hypotheses as still assumed.

At N = \omega the leading monomial of \delta is therefore (\log \omega)/\omega, which in the Berarducci--Mantova hierarchy [berarducci-mantova2018] sits strictly between grade -1 and grade 0: it exceeds c/\omega for every real c, and is exceeded by \omega^{-1+\varepsilon} for every real \varepsilon > 0. Two statements follow, and both are load-bearing:

  1. \mathrm{ord}_\omega(\delta) = -1 in the coarse grading. The remainder is a first-order infinitesimal, so \mathrm{st}(\delta) = 0 and the figure-eight discharge above is correct as stated.
  2. \delta is not a grade-(-1) monomial: \omega \cdot \delta is infinite. A grade-(-1) monomial c/\omega would give the finite \omega \cdot (c/\omega) = c.

Quoting only the first — "the remainder is a first-order infinitesimal" — is true and misleading. It is the second that records that the underlying convergence is logarithmically slow.

Three consequences, derived before measurement

Each consequence below was written down from the expansion above, and only then compared against this corpus's own Kashaev sum at N = 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600 (exact mpmath at 50 dps, with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) computed as 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) rather than read from a float literal).

What this prices

The algebra-versus-analysis table above assigns the whole analytic burden of the surreal form to a single application of \mathrm{st}, on the ground that the pre-\mathrm{st} side is exact rational arithmetic in \mathbf{No}. That accounting is unchanged, but the second row is not free: the object \mathrm{st} is applied to differs from \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) by a quantity whose \omega-multiple diverges, so the reduction is not the truncation of a convergent tail. The surreal form relocates the analysis into \mathrm{st} faithfully; it does not make it small.

Scope. This is an asymptotic statement about 4_1 alone, resting on a cited expansion that is not re-derived here. What is established is that this corpus's own computed Kashaev sum reproduces that expansion, and that the three consequences hold. It does not bear on the volume conjecture for any other knot, does not alter \mathrm{st}, and does not weaken the figure-eight discharge.

Connection to QOU

This paper uses the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture as a cross- check on its categorical mass formula (Kashaev volume--density). The mass formula computes a particle mass via Hoefsmit/Markov-trace data; the cross-check identifies this with a Jones-polynomial evaluation, which Kashaev relates to hyperbolic volume.

Under the surreal lift:

  • Hoefsmit/Markov-trace side lifts to \mathbf{No} exactly (algebraic).
  • Jones polynomial at q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R} lifts by definition (q_0 \in \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbf{No}).
  • Hyperbolic volume side stays in \mathbb{R} (external anchor).
  • Kashaev's identity, recast as a surreal standard-part identity, bridges the two.

If the surreal Kashaev conjecture is proved (or even just proved for the knot class relevant to QOU), the QOU mass formula acquires an algebraic foundation independent of hyperbolic geometry.

Proof strategy

Reformulation reducibility (provable now):

  1. Show: the classical Kashaev statement (limit form) and the surreal Kashaev statement (standard-part form) are equivalent — one holds iff the other does.

  2. Forward direction: if \lim_{n \to \infty} 2\pi \log |J_K(\zeta_n, n)|/n = \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K), then by the transfer principle the standard-part of the surreal evaluation matches.

  3. Backward direction: if \mathrm{st}(\cdots) = \mathrm{Vol}(\cdots), then by definition of \mathrm{st} the asymptotic limit converges to \mathrm{Vol}.

Verification on known cases (provable now):

  1. The figure-eight knot 4_1 (Murakami–Murakami 2001 [murakami-murakami2001]) and the trefoil 3_1 have the volume conjecture proved. Compute J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega) directly, take \mathrm{st}, and verify equality with the known volume.

  2. Express the surreal evaluations through Gonshor's sign-sequence map and the surreal \omega.

General case (open):

  1. The general Kashaev conjecture for hyperbolic knots is open classically. The surreal reformulation does not provide a new line of attack, but it separates the algebraic content (rational-in-\omega evaluations of J_K) from the geometric content (the volume identity).

Falsification path: identical to the classical Kashaev conjecture; if the limit form fails for some knot, the surreal form fails as well (and conversely).

Provability assessment: the equivalence of the two formulations is provable (transfer principle). The underlying conjecture is a long-standing open problem; the reformulation does not by itself solve it but reorganises the problem productively.
rem:perpetual-obstruction-depth-omega:
Remark The perpetual obstruction as a single surreal grade. The motivic perpetual obstruction theorem asserts that the aether's motivic Galois character is non-trivial at every finite place p \nmid \chi(A), so the obstruction \kappa_n is non-trivial at every Kummer level n \nmid \chi(A), an infinite (cofinite-density) set of levels; it vanishes at the finitely many n \mid \chi(A). Under the surreal lift, this infinite family of non-vanishing statements is the shadow of a single graded coefficient.

Recall the aether identification \varepsilon = q - 1 \leftrightarrow 1/\omega (surreal blow-up calculus), under which the level-n contribution sits at \varepsilon-order n. The element

  \varepsilon^{\omega} \;=\; \omega^{-\omega},
  \qquad
  0 \;<\; \varepsilon^{\omega} \;<\; \varepsilon^{n}
  \quad\text{for every finite } n,

is the unique grade lying beneath the entire finite tower — the depth-\omega slot of the Conway normal form. It exists in \mathbf{No} precisely because \mathbf{No} admits Hahn expansions with surreal exponents, and has no counterpart in the archimedean Hahn line \mathbb{R}((\varepsilon^{\mathbb{Q}})), whose exponents are finite.

Interpretation. Perpetuity of the obstruction is equivalent to the surreal-lifted obstruction \widehat{\kappa} carrying a non-zero component at the depth-\omega grade:

  \kappa_n \neq 0 \ \ (\forall\, n \in \mathbb{N})
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  [\varepsilon^{\omega}]\,\widehat{\kappa} \;\neq\; 0 .

The universally-quantified family collapses to one non-vanishing graded coefficient. def:categorical-mordell-weil:
Definition Invariant Hom-group, finite-place Euler product, and monoidal localisation kernel. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q and Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q (Descartes elliptic curve).

The invariant Hom-group of an object E_q \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathbf{C}) whose fibre-functor image is \tau(E_q) = H^1(\mathcal{E}_q, \mathbb{Z}) is

\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}) := \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, E_q),

with rank r_q := \mathrm{rank}\,\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}). Under Tannaka--Krein reconstruction (reconstruction), \mathbf{C} \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(G) identifies \mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}) \cong \tau(E_q)^G = H^1(\mathcal{E}_q)^G, the multiplicity space of the trivial representation \mathbf{1} in \tau(E_q). On the adjoint object \mathrm{Ad}(A) (and on any non-trivial irreducible G-representation such as V_{1/2} of \mathrm{SU}(2)), the categorical observability condition \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 forces r_q = 0. This invariant Hom-group is a representation-theoretic construction in \mathbf{C}, not the arithmetic Mordell--Weil group E(\mathbb{Q}) of rational points; for the rational elliptic curve Cremona 50\mathrm{a}1 associated with Bring's Jacobian, \mathrm{rank}\,E(\mathbb{Q}) = 0 is a classical theorem of Kolyvagin.

The finite-place Euler product attached to a finite set S of maximal ideals \mathfrak{m} \in \mathrm{Spec}(R_q) of Bring's coordinate ring, with local Frobenius pair \alpha_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathfrak{m}), \bar{\alpha}_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathfrak{m}) restricted from the local q-zeta function and norm N(\mathfrak{m}) = q^{f(\mathfrak{m})}, is

L_S(\mathcal{E}_q, t) := \prod_{\mathfrak{m} \in S} \frac{1}{1 - \alpha_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathfrak{m}) t_{\mathfrak{m}} + N(\mathfrak{m}) t_{\mathfrak{m}}^2}.

The monoidal localisation kernel for a family of localisation homomorphisms \mathrm{loc}_\rho \colon H^1_\otimes(\mathbf{C}, E_q) \to H^1_\otimes(\mathbf{C}_\rho, E_q) on first cohomology of the monoidal category is the subgroup intersection

\mathrm{Sha}_q(\mathcal{E}_q) := \ker\!\left( H^1_{\otimes}(\mathbf{C}, E_q) \longrightarrow \prod_{\rho} H^1_{\otimes}(\mathbf{C}_\rho, E_q) \right) = \bigcap_{\rho} \ker(\mathrm{loc}_\rho).
rem:categorical-sha-local-global: Remark The monoidal localisation kernel as a local--global invariant. The monoidal localisation kernel \mathrm{Sha}_q(\mathcal{E}_q) of the invariant Hom-group and localisation datum consists of global classes x \in H^1_\otimes(\mathbf{C}, E_q) satisfying \mathrm{loc}_\rho(x) = 0 at every index \rho. Over a finite-field fibre where \mathcal{E}_q \hookrightarrow \mathcal{B} is a genus-1 sub-curve, the restricted Frobenius eigenvalue on H^1(\mathcal{E}_q) has modulus q^{1/2} under Weil's hypotheses, so each quadratic factor 1 - \alpha_{\mathcal{E}} t + q t^2 has no root inside |t| < q^{-1/2}.
sec:laurent-syracuse-intro:
Write [2]_q = q + 1 and [3]_q = q^2 + q + 1 in the Laurent polynomial ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], where Bézout's identity [3]_q - q[2]_q = 1 makes [2]_q and [3]_q coprime. Define the partial affine [2]_q-division map \mathcal{C}_q on \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] by

\mathcal{C}_q(P) =
\begin{cases}
  P / [2]_q & \text{if } P(-1) = 0,\\[4pt]
  \bigl([3]_q P + 1\bigr) / [2]_q & \text{if } P(-1) = -1,
\end{cases}

and call a sequence (P_j)_{j \ge 0} domain-stable if P_j(-1) \in \{0, -1\} and P_{j+1} = \mathcal{C}_q(P_j) for all j \ge 0. The propositions below classify all periodic orbits of \mathcal{C}_q in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], show that evaluation at q = 1 projects any domain-stable sequence onto the integer Syracuse map n \mapsto n/2 or (3n + 1)/2, and prove by \mathbb{F}_2[q] reduction that every domain-stable sequence with bounded exponent window is eventually periodic.
def:two-q-adic-valuation:
Definition The [2]_q-adic valuation on the Skein module. For an element P \in \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] of the Skein module, define the [2]_q-adic valuation:

v_{[2]}(P) := \max\bigl\{k \geq 0 : [2]_q^k \mid P \text{ in } \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]\bigr\}.

This counts how many times [2]_q = q + 1 divides P in the Laurent polynomial ring. It is the q-analog of the 2-adic valuation v_2(n) that counts trailing zeros in the binary expansion of an integer.

The contact order of P with the [2]_q-divisor D_{[2]} = \{q : [2]_q = 0\} = \{-1\} is v_{[2]}(P), the multiplicity of vanishing of P(q) at q = -1.

At q = 1, [2]_1 = 2, and evaluation recovers the ordinary 2-adic valuation v_2(P(1)) whenever no additional cancellation mod 2 occurs.
prop:balanced-holonomy-exclusion:
Proposition Balanced-holonomy exclusion and periodic-orbit classification for \mathcal{C}_q on \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Let \mathcal{C}_q be the partial affine [2]_q-division map on \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].

  1. Balanced-holonomy exclusion. In any commutative ring where [2]_q = q + 1 is not a unit, the equation [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} = [2]_q^k has no solution with k_{\mathrm{odd}} \ge 1 and k \ge 1, so \mathcal{C}_q admits no periodic orbit of multiplicative holonomy A = [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} / [2]_q^k = 1 other than the fixed point \{0\}. Over \mathbb{R}_{>0}, although [3]_\rho^3 = [2]_\rho^5 holds at the real root \rho \approx 1.32472 of q^3 = q + 1, positivity of the additive holonomy B > 0 still excludes any non-zero balanced cycle.
  2. Complete cycle classification in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Across all multiplicative holonomies A in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], the only periodic orbits of \mathcal{C}_q are \{0\}, the odd fixed point \{-q^{-2}\}, and the 2-cycle \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\}.
prf:balanced-holonomy-exclusion:
Proof Proof of balanced-holonomy exclusion and Laurent cycle classification. The affine [2]_q-division map carries an additive shift on the non-divisible branch, \mathcal{C}_q(P) = ([3]_q P + 1)/[2]_q, and divides cleanly on the divisible branch, \mathcal{C}_q(P) = P/[2]_q. A periodic orbit of length k = k_{\mathrm{odd}} + k_{\mathrm{even}} satisfies \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = P. Iterating the affine branches yields

  \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = A\,P + B,
  \qquad
  A = \frac{[3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}}}{[2]_q^{k}},

where A = \prod_i a_i is the multiplicative holonomy and B = \sum_i \bigl(\prod_{j>i} a_j\bigr) b_i collects the additive shifts (b_i = 0 on divisible steps and b_i = 1/[2]_q > 0 on non-divisible steps at real q > 0). Periodicity is equivalent to the linear relation

  (1 - A)\,P = B.

Balanced holonomy (A = 1). Suppose [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} = [2]_q^{k}. Periodicity then forces B = 0. Whenever k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1, at least one b_i is nonzero, so B is a nonempty sum of products of rational functions in q with positive coefficients; consequently B > 0 at every real q > 0 and B \neq 0 in \mathbb{Q}(q) (evaluating at q = 1). Hence B = 0 fails both formally and at every real q > 0.

Over \mathbb{Z}[q], balanced holonomy with k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1 is already algebraically impossible: the Bézout identity

  [3]_q - q[2]_q = 1

gives \gcd([2]_q, [3]_q) = 1 in \mathbb{Z}[q], so [3]_q is a unit modulo [2]_q whereas [2]_q^k \equiv 0 \pmod{[2]_q} for k \geq 1. At isolated real specializations A = 1 can occur—for instance at the plastic number \rho > 1 satisfying \rho^3 = \rho + 1, where 1 + \rho + \rho^2 = \rho^5 and 1 + \rho = \rho^3 give [3]_\rho^{\,3} = \rho^{15} = [2]_\rho^{\,5}—and positivity of B excludes periodic orbits there as well. When k_{\mathrm{odd}} = 0, the iteration reduces to P/[2]_q^k = P, forcing P = 0. More generally, \gcd([a]_q, [a+1]_q) = [\gcd(a, a+1)]_q = 1 excludes non-trivial balanced-holonomy cycles across every consecutive q-integer affine map ([a]_q, [a+1]_q).

Affine holonomy (A \neq 1) in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. For k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], coprimality guarantees A \neq 1 and yields a unique candidate rational solution P_0 = B/(1 - A) \in \mathbb{Q}(q). Classifying which candidates lie in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] requires no positivity or archimedean specialization: write b = \operatorname{ord}_q P for a nonzero periodic element P \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], with \beta \neq 0 the coefficient of q^b and \beta' the coefficient of q^{b+1}. Because [2]_q = 1 + q has constant term 1, division by 1 + q preserves \operatorname{ord}_q, and so does P \mapsto ([3]_q P + 1)/(1 + q) whenever b < 0; thus b is constant along every cycle with b < 0.

  1. Case b \leq -2. A divisible step P = (1 + q)P' gives \beta'(P') = \beta' - \beta. A non-divisible step (1 + q)P' = [3]_q P + 1 leaves \beta' unchanged because [3]_q P has coefficients \beta and \beta + \beta' in degrees b and b + 1, while +1 sits in degree 0 > b + 1. Summing around a cycle with e divisible steps gives e\beta = 0, so e = 0. An all-non-divisible cycle satisfies (1 + q)D' = [3]_q D for D = P + q^{-2}, hence \bigl((1 + q)^k - [3]_q^k\bigr)D = 0; evaluating at q = 1 gives 2^k \neq 3^k, forcing D = 0 and P = -q^{-2}.
  2. Case b \geq 0. Every iterate lies in \mathbb{Z}[q], and evaluation at q = 0 gives P'(0) = P(0) on divisible steps and P'(0) = P(0) + 1 on non-divisible steps. Periodicity forces k_{\mathrm{odd}} = 0, and ((1 + q)^k - 1)P = 0 forces P = 0.
  3. Case b = -1. Setting S = qP \in \mathbb{Z}[q] turns the non-divisible step into (1 + q)S' = [3]_q S + q. If some iterate S along the cycle is a constant c \in \mathbb{Z}, degree considerations exclude a divisible step from c, and evaluating (1 + q)S' = [3]_q c + q at q = -1 forces c = 1, producing the 2-cycle S \in \{1,\, 1 + q\}, i.e. P \in \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\}. Otherwise every iterate satisfies \deg S = d \geq 1. Reversing polynomial coefficients sends (1 + q)S' = [3]_q S + q to (1 + q)\tilde{S}' = [3]_q \tilde{S} + q^{d+1} with d + 1 \geq 2, while palindromicity of 1 + q and [3]_q preserves divisible steps. The low-degree coefficient count of case 1 applied to the reversed sequence forces zero divisible steps, whence D = P + q^{-2} again satisfies \bigl((1 + q)^k - [3]_q^k\bigr)D = 0 and P = -q^{-2}, contradicting \operatorname{ord}_q P = -1.

Consequently \{0\}, \{-q^{-2}\}, and \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\} are the unique periodic orbits of \mathcal{C}_q on \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. \square
prop:q-syracuse-lift:
Proposition Evaluation at q = 1 projects \mathcal{C}_q-orbits to Syracuse trajectories and lifts periodicity. Let (P_j)_{j \ge 0} be a domain-stable sequence in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] under \mathcal{C}_q, and let \mathrm{ev}_1 \colon \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] \to \mathbb{Z} denote evaluation at q = 1, alongside the integer Syracuse map T(n) = n/2 (n even) and T(n) = (3n + 1)/2 (n odd) [lagarias2010].

  1. Projection to T. For every j \ge 0, \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j) is even on an even step ([2]_q P_{j+1} = P_j), odd on an odd step ([2]_q P_{j+1} = [3]_q P_j + 1), and satisfies \mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+1}) = T(\mathrm{ev}_1(P_j)).
  2. Parity periodicity implies Laurent periodicity. If the step-type sequence repeats with period K \ge 1 from index N onward, then P_{N+K} = P_N.
  3. Lifting eventual periodicity. If the integer trajectory \bigl(T^j(P_0(1))\bigr)_{j \ge 0} is eventually periodic, then (P_j) enters one of the three cycles \{0\}, \{-q^{-2}\}, or \{q^{-1}, 1 + q^{-1}\} classified in periodic-orbit classification.
prf:q-syracuse-lift:
Proof Proof of Syracuse projection and parity-periodicity lifting. Item 1. Applying \mathrm{ev}_1 to [2]_q P_{j+1} = P_j gives 2\,\mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+1}) = \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j), so \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j) is even and \mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+1}) = \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j)/2. Applying \mathrm{ev}_1 to [2]_q P_{j+1} = [3]_q P_j + 1 gives 2\,\mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+1}) = 3\,\mathrm{ev}_1(P_j) + 1, so \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j) is odd and \mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+1}) = T(\mathrm{ev}_1(P_j)).

Item 2. Set D_j = P_{N+K+j} - P_{N+j}. Because steps N + K + j and N + j have identical type, subtracting the two step equations cancels the +1 term:

[2]_q\, D_{j+1} = c_j\, D_j, \qquad c_j \in \{1, [3]_q\}.

Induction yields [2]_q^n D_n = \bigl(\prod_{j < n} c_j\bigr) D_0 for all n \ge 0. Since [3]_q - q[2]_q = 1, every c_j is coprime to [2]_q, so [2]_q^n \mid D_0 for every n \ge 0. Multiplying D_0 by a power of q to obtain a polynomial f \in \mathbb{Z}[q] with (q + 1)^n \mid f for every n forces f = 0 (otherwise n \le \deg f), hence D_0 = 0 and P_{N+K} = P_N.

Item 3. If T^{N+K}(n_0) = T^N(n_0) for n_0 = P_0(1) and K \ge 1, Item 1 gives \mathrm{ev}_1(P_{j+K}) = \mathrm{ev}_1(P_j) for all j \ge N, so the step types repeat with period K from N onward. Item 2 then gives P_{N+K} = P_N, placing P_N on one of the three periodic orbits of periodic-orbit classification. \square
prop:laurent-bounded-window:
Proposition Bounded-support \mathcal{C}_q-orbits enter a finite cycle via \mathbb{F}_2[q] pigeonhole. Let (P_j)_{j \ge 0} be a domain-stable sequence in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] under \mathcal{C}_q.

  1. Suppose there exist integers N_0, m \ge 0 such that q^{N_0} P_j \in \mathbb{Z}[q] has degree at most m for every j \ge 0. Then (P_j) reaches one of the three periodic orbits \{0\}, \{-q^{-2}\}, or \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\}.
  2. Equivalently, any domain-stable sequence that never enters one of those three orbits has unbounded exponent support and projects at q = 1 to a non-periodic, unbounded integer Syracuse trajectory.
prf:laurent-bounded-window:
Proof Proof of bounded-window convergence via \mathbb{F}_2[q] reduction. Item 1. Set f_j = q^{N_0} P_j \in \mathbb{Z}[q], so (q + 1) f_{j+1} = f_j on an even step and (q + 1) f_{j+1} = (q^2 + q + 1) f_j + q^{N_0} on an odd step, and write \bar{f}_j \in \mathbb{F}_2[q] for the reduction modulo 2:

  • Evaluating modulo 2 at q = 1 (where q + 1 = 0 and q^2 + q + 1 = 1 in \mathbb{F}_2) gives \bar{f}_j(1) = 0 on an even step and \bar{f}_j(1) = 1 on an odd step, so \bar{f}_j determines the step type.
  • Whenever \bar{f}_i = \bar{f}_j, steps i and j share the same type, so (q + 1)\bar{f}_{i+1} = (q + 1)\bar{f}_{j+1} in the integral domain \mathbb{F}_2[q]; cancelling q + 1 \neq 0 yields \bar{f}_{i+1} = \bar{f}_{j+1}.
  • Since \deg \bar{f}_j \le m, there are at most 2^{m+1} polynomials in \mathbb{F}_2[q] of degree at most m.

By the pigeonhole principle, \bar{f}_a = \bar{f}_c for some a < c, so \bar{f}_{a+k} = \bar{f}_{c+k} and the step types repeat with period c - a for all k \ge 0. Item 2 of Syracuse projection gives P_c = P_a, and periodic-orbit classification restricts P_a to the three listed cycles.

Item 2 is the contrapositive of Item 1 combined with Item 3 of Syracuse projection. \square
rem:algebraic-core-survives:
Remark The algebraic core of QOU lifts to any real-closed field. Archimedean specialisation. This survey justifies the central move: the aether parameter q \in \mathbf{No} may be taken in the infinitesimal neighbourhood of 1, without disturbing any algebraic machinery of this paper. The bulk of the formal structure is purely algebraic. It depends only on the ground ring being a field (typically of characteristic zero), independent of any analytic or topological property of \mathbb{R} or \mathbb{C}.

Blocks that lift verbatim

The following constructions are formulated over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], \mathbb{Q}(q), or an arbitrary characteristic-zero field, and therefore lift unchanged to any real-closed extension K \supseteq \mathbb{R}, in particular to \mathbf{No}:

  1. Hecke algebra H_n(q). The presentation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 plus the braid relations \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} makes sense over any commutative ring in which q is invertible. The Wedderburn decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} M_{d_\lambda}(K) holds at generic q over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

  2. Hoefsmit seminormal form (Hoefsmit seminormal form). The matrix entries of \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) are rational functions in q with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}. The eigenvalues q (symmetric channel) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric channel) are field-polymorphic.

  3. Markov trace and Jones polynomial. The unique trace \mathrm{tr}_M : H_\infty(q) \to K[q, q^{-1}] satisfying the Markov property yields the Jones polynomial J_K(q) as an element of \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]; nothing needs \mathbb{R}.

  4. q-Schur--Weyl duality. The decomposition of V^{\otimes n} into irreducible H_n(q)-modules indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n with at most two parts is purely representation-theoretic.

  5. q-deformed identities. c_q = 1/(q - 1), \hbar_q = (q-1)/q, [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}), [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^n [k]_q, and the quantum dimension \dim_q(\lambda) are all rational in q and lift unchanged to any field.

  6. Rigid monoidal category axioms (rigid monoidal category). The axioms of a strict rigid monoidal category (associator, unitors, left/right duals, evaluation/coevaluation) are categorical identities, not analytic conditions.

  7. Hopf algebra structure on \mathcal{H}_q. Comultiplication, antipode, coassociativity, and the grouplike elements \exp_q, \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q are all formal-power-series manipulations over any field.

  8. Frobenius algebra structure on A as a bare algebraic structure (the non-degeneracy of \int_A as a pairing A \otimes A \to K). This is a bilinear form condition and requires only a field.

  9. Braid group action: B_n acts on V^{\otimes n} via the Hecke R-matrix; the action is functorial in the ground ring.

  10. Character formulas: the Hoefsmit-Murphy formula for \chi_\lambda(\sigma_w) in terms of contents of the Young diagram is a rational-function identity.

  11. Elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q as an algebraic variety. The Descartes Weierstrass equation defines a smooth projective curve over K[q, q^{-1}] (away from the discriminant locus). Its group law is algebraic.

  12. Tannaka--Krein reconstruction of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) from (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau): the reconstruction procedure produces a Hopf algebra from a fibre functor to K-modules; the ground field plays no essential role beyond being a field.

  13. Rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet: the Van den Bergh duality isomorphism \omega_A^\bullet \simeq R\mathrm{Hom}_{A^e}(A, A^e) is a statement in derived algebra, unchanged over surreals.

  14. Fibre functor rigidity (deformation-theoretic): vanishing of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) is a cohomological condition independent of topology.

Note: Frobenius is a structural sieve, not a measure

Item 8 above can be mis-read. The Frobenius pairing \int_A : A \otimes A \to K on the QOU observable algebra is an algebraic bilinear form: a non-degenerate K-linear map witnessing the self-duality A \cong A^\vee as objects of the rigid braided monoidal category. It is not a Lebesgue-style measure-theoretic integral, and it is not a surrogate for one. The Costin–Ehrlich–Friedman theorem [costin-ehrlich-friedman2015] rules out any translation- invariant measure on the full ring C(\mathbf{No}), so no axiomatic stipulation could install one without contradicting a proved theorem.

What the Frobenius axiom does instead is select a sub-algebra of admissible observables. An object A in the monoidal category may only carry a Frobenius structure if it is rigid and self-dual; this is a strong constraint that excludes most of the wild functions in C(\mathbf{No}) (e.g. continuous surreal-valued functions with non-well-ordered support, or indicator functions of order-disconnected pieces of \mathbf{No}). The QOU observable algebra is built bottom-up from representation-theoretic data (H_n(q) modules, Wedderburn blocks, braid-word characters) — none of which can produce such pathological elements. This dissolves the apparent paradox "QOU has a Frobenius pairing on its observable algebra A, therefore QOU has a Lebesgue integral on C(\mathbf{No})": the algebra A is not C(\mathbf{No}), but the representation-theoretic sub-algebra generated by Hecke matrices and Markov-trace functionals, all of which live on the CEF-positive side of the integration partition (analytic / transseriable functions of q, evaluated at q = q_0 \in \mathbf{No}). The Frobenius pairing exists on it not because one was postulated on C(\mathbf{No}), but because the sub-algebra is small enough and algebraic enough to admit one.

Consequence for the appendix

The core mass formula — Hoefsmit seminormal form \to Markov trace \to Jones polynomial at the aether value — runs identically over \mathbf{No}. The categorical mass \mathfrak{m}(K), transfer matrix T(c,d), and q-value predictions are all field-polymorphic and have well-defined interpretations wherever q \in \mathbf{No} is chosen.

The break from \mathbb{R} to \mathbf{No} only becomes non-trivial at the last step: when a categorical quantity is compared to a measured real number, a standard-part must be taken (classical limit as standard-part).
prop:tarski-sign-decision-depth:
Proposition Finite-N signs are decided along the sign expansion, at a finite birthday. Let K be any ordered field and let \alpha \in K be a root of a rational polynomial p. Follow \alpha through Conway's sign-expansion recipe: start at 0; at each step compare \alpha with the current dyadic value v, take the sign + if v < \alpha and - otherwise, and move to the next dyadic of Gonshor's construction. After n signs, \alpha lies in a dyadic window \ell_n < \alpha \le h_n whose endpoints are born by day n.

Proposition. Let f \in \mathbb{Q}[x].

  1. (Each sign is a finite rational check.) If p has no zero on the half-window that does not contain \alpha, the next sign is determined. A certificate is a Bernstein form \sum_{i \le d} c_i (x - a)^i (b - x)^{d-i} of \pm p on [a, b] with c_i \ge 0 and c_0, c_d > 0 (or a Taylor shift \sum c_i (x - m)^i on a half-line). Checking it is a polynomial identity and finitely many inequalities between rationals.
  2. (Decision.) If f has such a certificate on [\ell_n, h_n], then 0 < f(\alpha). The least such n is the decision depth of the claim: the birthday of the coarsest dyadic window that decides it.
  3. (Locatedness without an axiom.) Once both \ell_n and h_n exist, each further sign halves the window. So the cut of \alpha by its windows is located in any Archimedean K: the Lawvere condition \mathrm{coev} = 0 holds as a theorem for finite-N algebraic quantities.

Nothing here uses the intermediate value theorem, a real closed field, or the hypothesis that every observable is located: \alpha is given, and only its location is refined.

Birthdays grade windows, not numbers. An irrational algebraic number, like every non-dyadic real, is born on day \omega, so the birthday cannot measure the complexity of \alpha itself. It does measure the finite part of the sign expansion that a given claim reads, and that is a natural number.

The embedding is a sign prefix. For c = \zeta_N + \zeta_N^{-1}, the choice \zeta_N = e^{2\pi i/N} is the choice of the largest root of the minimal polynomial \Psi_N of c. That choice is the shortest sign prefix whose window holds no other root of \Psi_N (the embedding depth). It is finite rational data; no cosine and no \pi enter.

def:ecalle-borel-resummation:
Definition Écalle–Borel resummation: the Borel transform \mathcal{B} and its lateral and median sums. Archimedean specialisation. A divergent Gevrey-1 asymptotic series acquires a canonical analytic meaning through the Borel transform and its Laplace–Borel sums [ecalle1981].

Definition

Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let

  \tilde f(z) = \sum_{n \geq 0} a_n \, z^{-n-1},
  \qquad a_n \in K,

be a formal power series at z = \infty. The formal Borel transform of \tilde f is

  \mathcal{B}\tilde f(\xi) = \sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{a_n}{n!} \, \xi^n ,

the coefficient-wise division a_n \mapsto a_n / n!. When \tilde f is Gevrey-1 — |a_n| \leq C \, n! \, A^{-n} for some C, A > 0 and K \subseteq \mathbb{C} — its coefficients grow at most geometrically, so \mathcal{B}\tilde f is a germ analytic on the disc |\xi| < A.

Lateral Laplace–Borel sums and Stokes rays

Suppose \mathcal{B}\tilde f continues analytically along the ray e^{i\theta} \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} with at most exponential growth. The lateral Laplace–Borel sum of \tilde f in the direction \theta is

  \mathcal{L}^{\theta} \tilde f(z)
  = \int_0^{e^{i\theta} \infty} \mathcal{B}\tilde f(\xi) \,
    e^{-z\xi} \, d\xi ,

analytic and asymptotic to \tilde f (Gevrey-1) on a half-plane bisected by the conjugate direction. A direction \theta is a Stokes ray when a singularity \omega of \mathcal{B}\tilde f lies on e^{i\theta} \mathbb{R}_{> 0}: the integral through \omega is obstructed, and only the two lateral sums \mathcal{L}^{\theta^+}, \mathcal{L}^{\theta^-} (deformed on either side of \omega) are defined. Their difference is exponentially small, of order e^{-\omega z} — the Stokes phenomenon.

Median resummation

The median resummation \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}} is the canonical average of the two lateral sums across a Stokes ray — in the simplest one-singularity case \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\theta^+} + \mathcal{L}^{\theta^-}\bigr), and in general the composition of a lateral sum with the half-power of the Stokes automorphism [ecalle1981]. For a series with real coefficients whose Stokes ray is the positive real axis, the median sum is the unique real and single-valued resummation.

Beyond a single series: trans-series

The definition above resums one Gevrey-1 series. A trans-series \Phi = \sum_{\ell \ge 0} y^{\ell} \varphi_\ell(g) adds a second layer. Its lateral resummation s_\pm(\Phi) = \sum_{\ell} y^\ell s_\pm(\varphi_\ell)(g) is itself an infinite sum over the non-perturbative sectors, and that sum is a potential new source of divergence even when every lateral sum s_\pm(\varphi_\ell) exists [arxiv-2302.08363v2, §2, eq. (2.5)]. Reorganising by a fixed power g^n gives the partial series G_n(y) = \sum_\ell a_{n,\ell}\, y^\ell with \Phi = \sum_n g^n G_n(y) [arxiv-2302.08363v2, eqs. (2.6)--(2.7)]; the convergence property the source studies is that the G_n converge with a common radius R, with a_{n,\ell} \sim \ell^{-b_n} R^{-\ell} expected generically [arxiv-2302.08363v2, eq. (2.8)]. That property is proved for nonlinear ODEs in the work the source cites, and the source examines QFT examples in which it holds; it is not implied by the single-series construction of this definition.
rem:analytic-obstructions:
Remark Analytic obstructions: what breaks under surreal replacement. Archimedean specialisation. A first pass at a surreal lift of QOU would catalogue the general-purpose obstructions — Lebesgue measure, Hilbert-space completion, hyperbolic geometry — that surreal numbers famously lack [alling1987]. An honest audit of the actual QOU content, however, finds that most of these obstructions are not triggered by the main paper. This remark records which obstructions genuinely bite and which are only apparent.

0. An audit, not an axiomatisation

The shortcut of axiomatising a single integration operator on \mathbf{No} is mathematically closed. Costin, Ehrlich, and Friedman [costin-ehrlich-friedman2015] prove a two-sided result on integration over the surreals:

  • Positive direction. A robust algebraic integral exists for the class of semi-algebraic, analytic, and Écalle–Borel transserial functions, obtained by routing through Hardy- field germs and the surreal–transseries correspondence [berarducci-mantova2018]. On this class the integral satisfies the standard properties (linearity, FTC, translation invariance).
  • Negative direction. Set-theoretic obstructions rule out extending the integral to a translation-invariant operator on the full ring C(\mathbf{No}) of continuous surreal-valued functions. The order topology on \mathbf{No} is totally disconnected, C(\mathbf{No}) contains functions whose "support" violates well-ordering, and no measure on C(\mathbf{No}) can simultaneously be translation-invariant, \sigma-additive, and non-degenerate.

No measure on all of C(\mathbf{No}) is postulated. That object does not exist. Manufacturing one via a categorical proxy (e.g. asserting the Frobenius pairing \int_A : A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} at A = C(\mathbf{No})) smuggles the obstruction into the axiom. Instead, each genuine use of an analytic structure in this paper is audited to determine whether the use lifts to \mathbf{No} on the CEF-positive side (algebraic / transserial) or requires a custom workaround. The audit follows.

1. Lebesgue measure: one genuine use, no others

Lebesgue, Haar, and Hausdorff measures are evaluated throughout this paper. Almost all instances are categorical or algebraic upon inspection:

See Table 1.

Net effect. The Möbius energy proof is the only block whose argument genuinely depends on Lebesgue measure, and it is used as a motivational cross-check rather than as a load-bearing step in the mass formula. The mass formula itself — Hoefsmit \to Markov trace \to Jones \to aether value \to categorical mass — never integrates.

2. Hilbert-space completion: stylistic, not load-bearing

Only one place in this paper writes down a Hilbert- space completion: Proof of Completeness of the knot-type eigenbasis (part 3 of the proof). The passage reads:

The direct limit \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} is a pre-Hilbert space whose completion \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phys}} is separable (each V^{\otimes n} is finite-dimensional). The union of the finite-dimensional subspaces V^{\otimes n} is dense by construction, and each is completely decomposed by (1). Hence the irreducible summands, indexed by knot types via the closure map, span a dense subspace.

Close reading shows that the only step that invokes Hilbert structure is the word dense in the final sentence. Everything else — the direct limit, the finite-dimensional decomposition, the knot-closure indexing — is pure algebra. The conclusion can be restated in its algebraic form without loss:

The irreducible summands span the algebraic direct limit \varinjlim V^{\otimes n}.

This is the statement actually used downstream. The Hilbert framing is a stylistic choice (anticipating a physical interpretation) rather than a load-bearing argument. No spectral theorem, functional calculus, or unitary representation is used anywhere in the paper; Hoefsmit's diagonalisation is an algebraic diagonalisation of a matrix over \mathbb{C}(q).

Consequence: the Hilbert obstruction is only an obstruction to future work (e.g. a rigorous scattering-pipeline formulation with physical Hilbert spaces). The current paper survives without it.

3. Genuine obstructions that remain

Three narrow obstructions do bite:

  1. Möbius energy integral. Requires Lebesgue on S^1 \times S^1 plus diagonal regularisation. A surreal Loeb-measure replacement is possible in principle (see calculus up to \varepsilon, §5), but is not automatic.

  2. Hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K). Used for cross-checking the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (Kashaev volume--density). Hyperbolic geometry requires conformal structure on \mathbb{CP}^1 and metric completion of a universal cover — neither is native to \mathbf{No}. A surreal reformulation is proposed in Kashaev surreal reformulation, but it trades the hyperbolic-volume problem for an asymptotic-surreal problem rather than solving it.

  3. Classical limit q \to 1, interpreted as a topological limit (classical limit functor). This is not so much broken as replaced: the classical limit becomes the standard-part of evaluation at q = 1 + \varepsilon (see classical limit as standard-part), which is an exact substitute, not a weakening.

4. Things that look like obstructions but are not

For bookkeeping, the following were considered and ruled out as obstructions after audit:

  • Haar on \mathrm{SU}_q(2) — not used computationally; the paper uses the Hopf-algebra counit and Hoefsmit seminormal form, both algebraic.
  • Julia set measure \mu_J — used only for interpretive language; the Hausdorff dimension is rational in q.
  • Convergence of q-dilogarithm products — only used as formal power series.
  • Smooth-manifold structure on M — the main paper treats M via the brane tower (algebraic) and the frame bundle \mathcal{S} (algebraically described). Smoothness is a convenience, not load-bearing.
  • Spectral decomposition of Hecke generators — Hoefsmit gives it algebraically over \mathbb{Q}(q^{1/2}).
  • \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) action on \mathbb{CP}^1 — used only in knot-complement discussion and Möbius energy setup; not load-bearing for the mass formula.

5. Revised summary

See Table 2.

Conclusion. The surreal lift preserves nearly all structure. With two narrow exceptions — the Möbius energy integral and the hyperbolic-volume side of the Kashaev comparison — every load-bearing step of the mass formula and categorical axioms transfers to \mathbf{No} without modification. The remaining work constructs new structures (birthday grading, \varepsilon-relaxed axioms, standard-part map) in the surreal ambient.

rem:ecalle-borel-resurgence-vocabulary:
Remark Surrounding resurgence vocabulary and the three "Borel"s. Archimedean specialisation. The operators below are not part of the Écalle–Borel resummation object; they are its surrounding resurgence vocabulary [ecalle1981], together with a disambiguation of the three unrelated "Borel"s in this paper.

Alien derivatives and the bridge equation

For a singularity location \omega of \mathcal{B}\tilde f, Écalle's alien derivative \Delta_\omega is a derivation on resurgent series measuring the singularity type of \mathcal{B}\tilde f at \omega; it vanishes iff the Borel transform is regular there. The bridge equation

  \Delta_\omega \tilde f = A_\omega \, \frac{\partial \tilde f}{\partial z}

links the alien derivations to the natural derivation, with the scalar A_\omega the Stokes constant at \omega; the collection \{A_\omega\} determines the Stokes automorphism and hence the lateral–median relations of the resummation.

Disambiguation: three unrelated "Borel"s

The transform is due to Émile Borel and belongs to resurgence theory. It is distinct from two other "Borel"s in this paper: the Borel regulator (Armand Borel) on K_3 appearing in Borel partial resolution and Borel–Zagier QOU volumes, and the Lie-theoretic Borel subalgebras of the q-oper chapter. Resummation statements bear neither on regulator transcendence nor on q-oper flag data, and the three senses must not be cross-linked.
prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action:
Proposition Archimedean \rho_\infty Habiro-tail action of 4_1 is \pi^2/5 (golden-ratio dilogarithm), distinct from the geometric \mathrm{Vol} face. Archimedean specialisation. Conditional on the standard dilogarithm functional equations. Let S(q) = \sum_{n\ge 0} \prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) be the 4_1 Kashaev–Habiro cyclotomic tail, evaluated at real q = e^{t} (the archimedean \rho_\infty face). Then:

  1. S is bar-even: S(q) = S(q^{-1}), since each factor (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) is invariant under q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}.
  2. S is an alternating asymptotic series with (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) = -4\sinh^{2}(jt/2); its optimal-truncation (minimal-term) resurgent action is 
      A_0 \;=\; -4\int_{0}^{\ln\varphi}\ln\!\bigl(2\sinh s\bigr)\,ds \;=\; \frac{\pi^{2}}{5},
    where \varphi = (1+\sqrt5)/2 is the golden ratio and the minimal term sits at \mathrm{arcsinh}(1/2) = \ln\varphi.

The evaluation reduces to the golden-ratio Landen dilogarithm value \mathrm{Li}_2(\varphi^{-2}) = \pi^{2}/15 - \ln^{2}\varphi, one of the classical closed-form values listed in [zagier-dilogarithm, §1]. It follows from Euler reflection, duplication, and Landen's identity at the golden points \psi+\psi^{2}=1, 1+\psi=\varphi, \psi/(1+\psi)=\psi^{2} (with \psi=\varphi^{-1}). Those three functional equations are recalled in [hakimoglu-brown2025, §1.1], whose own golden-ratio result is a different identity (\pi^2/100 as the real part of \mathrm{Li}_2 at a root of a quartic, §6).

Two faces of the same quantum object. The 4_1 quantum dilogarithm admits two distinct archimedean evaluations, which do not coincide:

Face Evaluation Trace field Resurgent action
Geometric / state-integral Faddeev \Phi_b at the aether b (root-of-unity / Kashaev) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi \approx 0.646
Archimedean \rho_\infty real-q Habiro tail S(q) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5) \pi^{2}/5 \approx 1.974

The classical dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2 is the semiclassical (b\to 0) leading term of \Phi_b in both cases, but at different arguments — the geometric shape e^{i\pi/3} (giving \mathrm{Vol}, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})) versus the golden ratio \varphi^{-2} (giving \pi^{2}/5, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)). That the two faces carry different actions in different number fields is the \hbar \leftrightarrow 2\pi i/N resummation wall made exact: the state-integral and real-q Habiro evaluations are related by resummation, not by term-by-term reparametrisation.

Scope. This is a rigorous statement about the archimedean \rho_\infty (real-q) face. Because S is bar-even, the 4_1 Habiro tail carries no bar-odd datum, consistent with 4_1 amphichirality; the bar-odd (chiral) resurgence relevant to the Q_\beta odd channel must come from a chiral knot such as 5_2. Whether the real-q face — as opposed to the geometric state-integral face — is the physically relevant \rho_\infty evaluation for the Q_\beta observable is an open question; this proposition asserts only the mathematical identity, not a physical identification.

Relation to the proved resurgence results. The standard dictionary behind item 2 runs from a Habiro-ring element \Phi_K to the formal series F_K(x) = \Phi_K(e^{-1/x}) \in \mathbb{C}[[1/x]], its Borel transform G_K, and the median resummation S^{\mathrm{med}}_K; the Costin--Garoufalidis conjecture asks that G_K be resurgent, that S^{\mathrm{med}}_K be analytic on \mathrm{Re}\,x > 0 with radial limits at \tfrac{1}{2\pi i}\mathbb{Q}, and that those limits recover \Phi_K at roots of unity [crew2023, §1, eqs. (1.3)--(1.8) and Conj. 1.1]. Crew, Fantini, Goswami, Osburn and Wheeler prove the resurgence and median-resummation statements for Habiro elements that come from radial limits of partial theta series through a strange identity [crew2023, Thm. 1.2], and deduce the conjecture for the torus-knot families T(2,2u+1) and T(3,2^k) [crew2023, Cor. 1.5 and §3]. The hyperbolic knot 4_1 is not in that class, and the source supplies no strange identity for its tail, so the proved resurgence does not transfer to item 2: the action A_0 = \pi^2/5 above is an optimal-truncation statement about the real-q series and is not a consequence of [crew2023].

The state-integral face in the literature. The geometric face of the table is treated on the q-difference side by Garoufalidis and Wheeler, who work out the 4_1 equation tq\,f(qt;q) + (1-2t)\,f(t;q) + tq^{-1} f(q^{-1}t;q) = 0 completely: its solutions at t = 0 and t = \infty, their monodromy, residues and determinants, the associated state integral, the x-deformation, and an analytic lift of the colored Jones polynomial [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §1.5, Thm. 1.7, and \S§5.1--5.8]. That treatment concerns the state-integral face only; it makes no statement about the real-q tail S(q) of item 2.

Extension across the double-twist family. For the double-twist knots K(m,-p) (m,p \ge 1, with K(1,-1) = 4_1), the Lauridsen cyclotomic expansion and the q-hypergeometric Kontsevich--Zagier / strongly-unimodal root-of-unity dualities F_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = U_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) and \mathcal{F}_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = \mathcal{U}_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) of Lovejoy and Osburn [lovejoy-osburn, Thms. 1.1--1.2, Cors. 1.3--1.4, eq. (1.2)] write the real-q Habiro tail as \sum_{n\ge 0} C_{K(m,-p),n}(q)\prod_{j=1}^n (1-q^j)(1-q^{-j}). Under q \mapsto q^{-1} the Gaussian q-binomial chains swap m and p, giving C_{K(m,-p),n}(q^{-1}) = C_{K(p,-m),n}(q): bar-evenness therefore holds for the entire amphichiral diagonal K(m,-m) (including 8_3 = K(2,-2)), whereas off-diagonal knots such as 6_1 = K(1,-2) acquire a non-zero bar-odd part and asymmetric q > 1 versus q < 1 optimal-truncation actions. Unlike bar-evenness, the golden-ratio action \pi^2/5 is specific to the m = p = 1 base case where C_{K(1,-1),n}(q) = 1: on the q > 1 ray of K(2,-1) = 6_1^* (equivalently q < 1 of 6_1) the q^{n_1^2 + n_1} weight shifts the dilogarithm saddle to \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}) at e^{u^*} = 1 + 1/\sqrt{2}, giving the exact octagonal action \pi^2/8, whereas the q > 1 ray of 6_1 (A_0^+ \approx 1.6433) and the amphichiral knot 8_3 = K(2,-2) (A_0 \approx 0.9913, distinct from \mathrm{Vol}(8_3)/\pi \approx 1.6648) are governed by a quartic inner saddle whose optimal-truncation actions are \mathbb{Q}-linearly independent of \pi^2 up to norm 10^4.
def:standard-part-functor:
Definition standard-part map \mathrm{st} : \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R}. Archimedean specialisation. The standard-part map realizes the quotient \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} / \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}} \cong \mathbb{R} and underlies the classical limit at q = 1 + \varepsilon; its construction begins with the finite and infinitesimal surreals.

An element x \in \mathbf{No} is finite if there exists n \in \mathbb{N} with |x| \leq n. Write \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \subset \mathbf{No} for the subring of finite surreals, and \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}} \subset \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} for the ideal of infinitesimals (those x with |x| < 1/n for every n \in \mathbb{N}).

Definition

The standard-part map

  \mathrm{st} : \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R}

sends each finite surreal x to the unique real r \in \mathbb{R} with x - r \in \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}}. Classically [robinson1966, alling1987]:

  \mathrm{st}(x) =
  \sup\{q \in \mathbb{Q} : q \leq x\}
  = \inf\{q \in \mathbb{Q} : q \geq x\}.

The map \mathrm{st} is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}}, inducing a ring isomorphism

  \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} / \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}}
  \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbb{R}.

Functorial extension

For a K-linear category \mathbf{C} equipped with a birthday grading, define the standard- part functor

  \mathrm{St} : \mathbf{C}_{\leq \omega + 1}^{\mathrm{fin}}
   \longrightarrow \mathbf{C}_{\mathbb{R}}

from the finite-coefficient sub-category at birthday \leq \omega + 1 to the archimedean sub-category. On objects it is the identity; on morphisms it applies \mathrm{st} entrywise to the matrix representation of f in any Hoefsmit-type basis.

The standard-part map \mathrm{st} (standard-part functor) and the median resummation \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}} of Écalle–Borel resummation compute the same value wherever both are defined. This remark records the identification once, at block level; elsewhere it appears only in passing inside the surreal Kashaev reformulation.

Concretely: let \tilde f be a Gevrey-1 transseries whose Borel transform admits lateral Laplace sums along a Stokes ray. The two lateral sums \mathcal{L}^{\theta^\pm}\tilde f disagree by exponentially small terms; the median sum \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}}\tilde f is the unique real single-valued average. On the surreal side, the same \tilde f is a transseries in the sense of Berarducci–Mantova [berarducci-mantova2018], hence evaluates at a positive infinitesimal (or, for asymptotic-in-n series, at n = \omega) to a finite element of \mathbf{No}, and \mathrm{st} projects that element to \mathbb{R}.   \mathrm{st}\bigl(\tilde f\,\big|_{\,\varepsilon}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}}\tilde f ,
